what: Marc Lou vibe-coded MailCheap, an open-source newsletter platform with Claude Opus, priced per emails sent (cheaper than Beehiiv), with MCP/agentic features. Hit ~$860-1320 MRR in 9-10 days with 30-40 subscriptions, Stripe-verified via TrustMRR. Open-sourced after user requests.
why_us: Strong validation of AI-assisted rapid SaaS building for paid products in a competitive category (newsletters). Combines open-source, low cost, agent-ready (MCP), and fast revenue. Prior audience helped, but demonstrates speed of AI coding + distribution.

what: SleepSense (sleep tracker app) reportedly hit 200K downloads and $80K MRR in 89 days, driven primarily by AI-generated UGC videos (AI doctor clips and screen recordings with voiceovers highlighting snoring/farts).
why_us: High-revenue example of AI video marketing scaling a consumer app in the sleep/wellness niche. Shows low-cost AI content ($2-6/video) outperforming traditional UGC for acquisition.

what: Discord users frustrated by lack of a general notifications tab: app beeps frequently with no indication of which server/channel the notification is from. 'Why is there no general notifications tab?'
why_us: High-engagement (500+ likes) UX pain in a massively popular app. Opportunity for better client, extension, or alternative with superior notification management.

what: Users request a 'Shazam for movies': take a photo of a scene and identify the movie title. Specific feature request with engagement.
why_us: Clear, concrete product idea for visual search/identification tool. AI vision makes this buildable now; demand from casual users.

what: Boring/simple directory sites generating solid revenue: examples include OpenAlternative at $6,500 MRR, and mentions of plain directory sites doing $6,500/mo while pure AI automation did only $75. Low-barrier SEO + listings model.
why_us: Repeatable micro-SaaS model (directories) that works with minimal features, validated by multiple indie reports. Easy to niche down with AI for content/SEO.
engagement: High community interest in directory models

what: High engagement request for a dating app specifically for people who like fat guys. 'i wish there was a dating app for people who like fat guys im so tired'
why_us: Massive engagement (nearly 5k likes) on a niche dating vertical. Indicates underserved preference segment in dating apps; potential for specialized matching.

what: Small AI-powered tools and wrappers showing revenue: e.g., PDF tools at $2.1k MRR, volume boosters at $345 MRR with 80% growth, and various indie SaaS hitting $500-$2k MRR quickly.
why_us: Micro-SaaS and single-feature AI tools continue to monetize in 2026 despite oversupply narratives. Focus on specific pain points (PDF, audio) works.
engagement: Summary of multiple TrustMRR verified apps
